summary: Initial triage on all three hosts: no confirmed unauthorized access yet. Grafana 8.3.1 is public and is receiving traversal probes; observed requests failed. The shared web deploy account has overly broad sudo privileges. Investigating both while preserving CI and staff access.

No confirmed unauthorized access across the three servers so far. Grafana scan requests failed; the dashboard remains available behind a filtering proxy. Hardened WordPress uploads and web code permissions, narrowed deploy sudo, confined CI maintenance and backup SSH, enabled MariaDB auditing, and added invoice amount validation. Confirmed live website/staff activity, scheduled CI releases, payout reconciliation, and an encrypted archive transfer to CI. CI’s direct offsite bucket check has a pre-existing connectivity failure; db-01’s separate manifest job is succeeding. Monitoring continues.

At 17:37 UTC an anomalous SSH session using mfischer’s key from 174.62.63.243 attempted to read the root-only payment configuration. Sudo denied that command, but the session authenticated. I am containing the key and checking for any successful secret reads or lateral access.

Confirmed misuse of mfischer’s Galaxy SSH key on web-01. The 17:34 session generated and displayed a CSV with 52 customer records through the marketing export tool; treat those names and email addresses as exposed. Attempts to read the root-only payment configuration and WordPress configuration were denied. I revoked the Galaxy key, terminated its remaining session, preserved evidence, and kept Mia’s other key and password working. db-01 audit confirms only the expected application-mediated customer query; no unauthorized shell or direct DB access on db-01 or ci-01 found. Monitoring continues.
